chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Louis Armstrong's dedication to entertaining and his full laugh
summary: Milt calls Louis the most dedicated man he worked with, and Danny remembers his full laugh on stage.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: There's nothing... I can't possibly, in any way... The most amazing man I ever worked with in my life was Louis Armstrong. To see him... To see the dedication. I don't know of anybody that was dedicated to music, to entertaining people as this man was. His whole being was to entertain and serve the public.

You always saw him smile, and he'd laugh... He gave you a full laugh. Now, people get annoyed about that. He laughed, and his face, his muscles in his face... His whole face gave you a laugh. It wasn't a half-laugh, a jive laugh or a make-believe laugh. "How ya doin', Daddy." It was a whole, full laugh. Now, maybe it was different if you worked with him. But he'd give them people, everybody when he smiled... When he went out on stage and they'd give him the ovation, he leaned his head back with his handkerchief and his horn, and laughed.
